podcast.body: Puff Daddy and Ma$e's 1997 hit, constructed from two prior hits and borrowing its title from Matthew Wilder's 1984 hit "Break My Stride." The song also prominently sampled Grandmaster Flash & The Furious Five's 1982 single "The Message." This "hip hop Frankenstein's monster" spent six weeks at number one, surpassing the chart performance of both original songs. "The 1997 Puff Daddy and Mace Hit, can't nobody hold me down, was built out of two prior hits, and it borrowed its title from one of the songs Puffy is Interpolated."
